clue.text: At end of year, electricity suddenly goes off

parts.note: December, abbreviated DEC, is the last month of the year
electric current is measured in amps

explanation.surface: On New Year's Eve the power fails without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave abruptly, often secretly, so it means to go off suddenly.

clue.text: Food a nymph gives a snake

parts.note: ham is a common food
a dryad is a tree nymph of Greek myth

explanation.surface: A mythical spirit hands a meal over to a serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the name of a wood nymph, which adds to the misdirection, but here it is the king cobra.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamadryad is another name for the king cobra, a large venomous serpent.

clue.text: Bear hug for redhead by the shore

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap around, so the word for bear goes around the other piece

parts.note: to bear something is to stand it
the head, or first letter, of red is R

explanation.surface: Someone on the beach is embraced on account of their red hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a literary word for a beach or the land beside water.

clue.text: Decreases in quantity, as a result of docker's work

definitions.text: as a result of docker's work
definitions.meaning: someone who docks an animal cuts its tail short, leaving the tail removed

explanation.surface: Trade falls away because of what dock labourers have done.
explanation.walkthrough: The docker is not a port worker but someone who docks (cuts short) animals' tails.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to dwindle gradually, and literally describes tails removed by docking.

clue.text: A specific trio or just any folk?

definitions.meaning: three particular men named by their forenames
the idiom for ordinary people in general, anybody at all

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for anyone at all happens to be a list of three particular male names.

clue.text: Popular banker, but ill-mannered

parts.note: something in fashion is said to be in
a banker here is a stretch of water with banks; the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England

explanation.surface: A well-liked financier who is nonetheless rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is crossword slang for a river or channel, something that has banks, not a financier.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent means rudely disrespectful, a strong form of bad manners.

clue.text: Urges on the team

definitions.meaning: drives a horse forward with ..., hence encourages
The nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club

explanation.definitionFit: To spur is to goad onward, and Spurs is the familiar name of Tottenham Hotspur football club.

clue.text: A garland's so often made from it

indicators.note: the answer is made out of these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark on what wreaths are typically made of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made from it' reads as describing the garland's material but signals that SO OFTEN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A festoon is a chain of flowers or ribbons hung in a curve between two points.

clue.text: Leave the half-dead bit

indicators.note: half of the word dead is taken, its first two letters

parts.note: a part is a bit of something

explanation.surface: An instruction to abandon the portion that is barely alive.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to go away, which is to leave.

clue.text: Union put squeeze on the rat

parts.note: MU is the Musicians' Union
to squash is to squeeze

explanation.surface: A trade union put pressure on a turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' suggests a traitor or informer in the surface, but means the animal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Musquash is another name for the muskrat, a large North American water rodent.

clue.text: Dance with Arab in the desert

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as Arab in the sand

parts.note: a desert is a land of sand
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dance performed by an Arab out in the dunes.
explanation.definitionFit: The saraband is a slow stately Spanish dance in triple time.

clue.text: Supple and so slim, too

indicators.note: something supple bends and changes shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Praise of someone both flexible and slender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supple' is both the definition and the sign to bend SO SLIM into a new order; the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissom means lithe and slender, gracefully flexible.

clue.text: Crop said to be mixed and scattered

indicators.note: the letters are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: Farm produce reportedly of mixed kinds spread over the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a sound signal but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means occurring here and there, irregularly scattered.

clue.text: Sort of heather used for lighting fires

parts.note: a sort is a kind
ling is the common heather plant

explanation.surface: A type of moorland heather people burn to start a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindling is small dry wood or twigs burnt to get a fire going.

clue.text: Rake out entire library first

indicators.note: the abbreviation for library is placed at the front of the rest
out signals that the letters of entire are disordered

explanation.surface: An order to clear the whole library with a garden rake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' looks like a garden tool but is the definition, a dissolute man; 'out' signals the rearranged letters and 'first' puts the library abbreviation at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute man, which is what a libertine is.

clue.text: Will it make the doctor perfect?

definitions.text: Will it make the doctor perfect?

parts.words: Will it make the doctor perfect?
parts.note: plays on the saying that repetition makes perfect, and on a doctor's surgery business having the same name

explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's practice is their surgery, and practice, as the proverb says, makes perfect.

clue.text: Orangeman?

parts.note: read as two halves: a small citrus fruit, and a man who was an official of imperial China

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a citrus fruit and a high-ranking Chinese official, so it is literally an orange and a man.

clue.text: To obtain this fruit, turn to Capri

indicators.note: turn signals that the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to visit an Italian island to get fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn to' reads as 'go to', but 'turn' rearranges TO CAPRI.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Perambulates along street walks in nautical fashion

parts.note: a sailor rolls as he walks, with a swaying gait

explanation.surface: Someone walks down the road swaying like a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To perambulate is to walk about, which is what someone does who strolls.

clue.text: Emphasised rejection of puddings

indicators.note: rejection throws the word back, so it is read backwards

parts.note: something emphasised is stressed

explanation.surface: A firm refusal of sweet dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Desserts are sweet courses, which the British call puddings.

clue.text: Drink and put an end to things

definitions.meaning: to ... a plan or rumour is to stop it

explanation.definitionFit: Scotch is whisky, and to scotch something is to quash it.

clue.text: Channel Isles harbour to windward, following this imaginary circle

indicators.note: going to windward is going back against the wind, so both pieces are read backwards

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: Sailing directions from a Channel Islands harbour into the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are turned: PORT becomes TROP and CI becomes IC.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics are lines of latitude drawn on maps, imaginary circles around the globe.

clue.text: Pain a knife produced

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp pain

explanation.surface: A knife was drawn and caused pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A panga is a broad-bladed African machete.

clue.text: Ban root I used to bring about a miscarriage

indicators.note: the letters are used up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone banned a root once employed to end pregnancies.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscarriage is the loss of a pregnancy, and the answer can name the same thing in medical use.

clue.text: It's worse than inadequate, but using pole, is able to row

parts.note: S is the South Pole
someone who can is able
a tier is a row of seats

explanation.surface: Someone who can manage a boat with a pole is better than inadequate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests rowing a boat but is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: More scant means falling further short, so it is worse than merely inadequate.

clue.text: Flowers that are man-made

definitions.meaning: things that flow, that is, waterways

explanation.definitionFit: Canals are artificial waterways, things that flow and were built by people.

clue.text: You start to acquire skills, backing this scheme

indicators.note: going backwards, so the whole string of pieces is read in reverse
the start of the word is its first letter

parts.note: to get is to acquire
arts are skills

explanation.surface: Advice that a learner should pick up skills as part of a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the whole run of pieces around, so the answer is read from the end of skills back to the first letter of You.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is a plan of action, a scheme.
